summary: Martin King Whyte is a scholar of Sinology and sociology. He studied at Cornell and Harvard, where he earned a PhD in sociology. He taught at Michigan (1970–1994), George Washington (1994–2000), and Harvard, where he became professor emeritus in 2000.

Martin Lehnert works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Freiburg and held a post at the University of Munich as Professor of East Asian Religion and Philosophy, attested in 2016.

Martin Lowenthal is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche and Namkhai Norbu. He held posts at Boston College and Harvard University.

Martin Riesebrodt was a religious studies scholar. He studied at Tübingen, Berlin, Heidelberg (Promotion 1973), and Munich (Habilitation 1990). He served on the faculty at Munich (~1986–1990), Chicago (1990–2011; Divinity School ~1990–2014), and the Graduate Institute in 2013.

Martin Seeger is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Hamburg in 2004 under doctoral supervisor Barend Jan Terwiel. He held an attested post at the University of Hamburg in 2004.

Martin T. Adam is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at McGill University (PhD attested 2002) under Richard P. Hayes. He also studied at the CIHTS and with teachers including Kawamura, Tillemans, Katsura, Mishra, and Aklujkar.

Martin Willson was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Yeshe Thubten, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Geshe Thubten Loden, Zasep Tulku Rinpoche, Geshe Rabten, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Geshe Lhundub Sopa.

Martina Draszczyk is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under MA supervisor Lambert Schmithausen, completed her Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna (attested 2012), and held a post at the University of Vienna.

Martino Dibeltulo works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a PhD at the University of Michigan (attested 2015) under doctoral supervisor Donald S. Lopez, Jr., and also studied under mentor Ester Bianchi.

Marvin Eisenberg was an art historian who studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1939–1943) and Princeton University (~1946–1954). He held a post at the University of Michigan from approximately 1949 to 1983.

Mary C. Wright was a scholar of Sinology and history. After attending Ramsay High School, she studied at Vassar College (~1934–1938), Radcliffe College, and Harvard University (~1938–1951). She held faculty posts at Stanford (1947) and Yale (1959).

Mary Clabaugh Wright was a historian and Sinologist who studied at Vassar (1934–1938) and Radcliffe (MA ~1939, PhD ~1951). She was curator of the Hoover Institution's China collection (~1946–1959) and became an associate (1959) and full professor (1964) at Yale.

Mary Evelyn Tucker is a scholar of religious studies, Sinology, and Japanology. Educated at SUNY Fredonia, Fordham, Sophia, and Columbia (PhD), she held posts at Bucknell (1989–2005), UC Berkeley, Harvard (~2005–2006), and Yale (~2006).

Mary Haas was a linguist who studied at Earlham College (~1926–1930), the University of Chicago (~1930–1931), and Yale University (~1931–1935), working under Edward Sapir (~1930–1935). She held a post at UC Berkeley from ~1947 to 1977.
Mary Jaksch is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at the University of Sunderland under Peter Harvey (attested 2007) and trained under traditional teacher Ross Bolleter.

Mary Shepherd Slusser was an archaeologist and Indologist. She studied at Michigan, NYU, Harvard, and Columbia (PhD ~1950). She worked as a State Department research analyst (1951–1958) and held posts at the National Museum of African Art and Asian Art.
Marybeth White is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. She earned a double major honors degree from York University and was a doctoral candidate at Wilfrid Laurier University (attested 2006).

Maryla Falk was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She held a post at the University of Warsaw (~1937–1939), was a member of the Polish Oriental Society (1938), and became a Fellow of the Royal Asiatic Society (1974).

Marylin Martin Rhie is a scholar of Buddhist studies, art history, and Sinology who studied under mentors Harrie Vanderstappen and Pramod Chandra. She held an attested post as professor at Smith College in 1986.

Masaaki Chikusa was a scholar of Sinology, history, and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at Kyoto University, where he also held posts in 1968 and 1981–1993, before serving as professor at Otani University (~1993–2001).
